title: Normalized raw adic comparison transport
statement: Fix finite-field datum D, a prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Omega of Q_l and the data interfaces [def-zl-raw-heart-adic-lisse-data]. For any prescribed lisse realization family a satisfying Normalized, any normalized completed-system family c, any identity-induced coefficient comparison system S satisfying FdComparisonSchemeCoherence, and any continuous realization family r, there is a ClassicalFamily b over a and c. For every finite E and every separated finite-type geometric base Y there are CondensedCoefficients with the fixed pointwise formulas. On every Y the prescribed S, r and a admit HeartComparison (all finite and common bounds, derived realization and fibres). On every Y the same b admits ClassicalCommon with the normalized transitions, algebraic-model objects and maps, and full faithfulness. No heart object, strata or Weil structures are selected by this assertion.

proof.text: Identify E with its ULift by down, transporting its valuation ring and all finite quotients by this same algebra equivalence. Evaluation on a pro-etale chart identifies the rational and integral coefficient sheaves pointwise, and the inclusion square commutes because both maps take an integral value to that same field value. For the small condensed chart, use a small presentation of the finite extension; its valuation topology has clopen balls, so the continuous chart comparison applies. The same evaluation formulas give the two displayed section normalizations. Transport the finite-free normalized towers of the classical-system realization through these coefficient equivalences. Realize a tower by the degree-zero inverse limit followed by raw rationalization. The completed-system comparison and raw lisse realization identify its sheaf with the localization of that same limit; full faithfulness follows from their Hom bijections. Evaluation of the limit at a geometric point gives the required fibre comparison. Pullback and scalar extension use the quotient and balanced-tensor maps; their section formulas give exactly the pull_sections and scalar_sections fields, including the identity-chart projection. At common stages transport these finite functors and their scalar comparisons; the identity and associator laws descend to the pair categories. The classical functor is the existing algebraic-model functor on representatives and arrows, and its full faithfulness is the directed colimit of the finite Hom bijections. Finally the normalized heart-model comparison identifies both halves in each degree. Its identity-on-integral realization and the scalar-localization universal property identify its derived realization with a.J, and its point comparison gives fibres. All constructions preserve zero and require no nonempty base or positive rank.
